items.diagram_kind: projective-bundle Chow decomposition and pushforward identities
items.reason: The statement gives a graded direct-sum isomorphism built from pullback and powers of the tautological class, together with pushforward identities. A diagram can display how the summands map into the common Chow group and how fibre integration detects the top power. The current rendered item has no diagram. This is an editorial aid; the source formulas are already explicit and no mathematical defect is alleged.

claim_lines.text: be the projective bundle in the quotient convention, with tautological quotient

1.1 Pushforward identities. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an integral closed subscheme of dimension $m$, so that $\pi^*[V]=[\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_V)]$ is an $(m+r-1)$-cycle. First suppose $\mathcal E|_V$ is trivial. The zero schemes of $r-1$ coordinate sections of $\mathcal O(1)$ are relative hyperplanes meeting in a section $\sigma:V\to\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_V)$, so $\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*[V]=\sigma_*[V]$ and $\pi_*\sigma_*[V]=[V]$. For any $\mathcal E$ and $0\le s<r-1$, the cycle $\xi^s\cap\pi^*[V]$ has dimension $m+r-1-s>m$ and is supported on $\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_V)$, whose image has dimension $m$; hence its components push to zero by [L4]. For the top power with general $\mathcal E$, choose a dense open $U\subseteq V$ trivializing the bundle. The identity $\pi_*(\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*[V])=[V]$ holds over $U$, and its difference is in $A_m(V)$ supported on $V\setminus U$. This complement has dimension less than $m$, so localization [L3] makes the difference zero. Both identities extend by linearity to all $\alpha\in A_*(X)$. [L1, L2, L3, L4, given, algebra]

2.1 Injectivity. Suppose $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\xi^i\cap\pi^*\alpha_i=0$. Applying $\pi_*$ and step 1.1 gives $\alpha_{r-1}=0$, since the other summands push to zero. Capping the remaining relation with $\xi^j$ and applying $\pi_*$ successively gives $\alpha_{r-1-j}=0$ for every $0\le j\le r-2$ by the same computation, using associativity of repeated caps from [L2]. Hence the displayed map is injective. [L2, step 1.1, algebra]

objects: homological Chow groups A_{d+i}(X) for 0 ≤ i ≤ r−1
maps_and_relations: π: P(E) → X is the bundle projection; use the quotient convention π*E → O_{P(E)}(1), and set ξ = c1(O(1)).
For each i, map α_i ∈ A_{d+i}(X) to ξ^i ∩ π*α_i ∈ A_{d+r−1}(P(E)); the direct sum of these maps is the isomorphism in the statement.
Show fibre integration π_*: A_{d+r−1}(P(E)) → A_d(X) alongside the identities π_*(ξ^s ∩ π*α)=0 for s<r−1 and π_*(ξ^{r−1} ∩ π*α)=α.
Optionally show the fibre P^{r−1} over x and ξ as the hyperplane class, with ξ^{r−1} integrating to 1; retain a fibrewise/local picture as illustration of the pushforward formula, not as its proof.
checks: Rank is r and relative dimension is r−1; the powers in the decomposition run from i=0 through r−1.
Flat pullback raises homological dimension by r−1, and capping with ξ^i lowers it by i: A_{d+i}(X) maps into A_{d+r−1}(P(E)).

Proper pushforward preserves cycle dimension (and is zero if the image dimension drops), so π_* of the displayed target lies in A_{d+r−1}(X); in the top-power identity the input ξ^{r−1} ∩ π*α has the same dimension as α and pushes to α.
The top power is ξ^{r−1}, not ξ^r, for the quotient projective bundle convention and fibre dimension r−1.

Do not depict one pushforward as independently extracting every α_i. After the top coefficient is detected, coefficient recovery proceeds successively on the remaining relation; higher powers can contribute during this triangular elimination.

The Chow groups are homological in the general statement; codimension grading applies only under the stated smooth equidimensional hypothesis. No sign appears in these ordinary Chow pushforward identities.
